t: American code breakers had partly read the Japanese naval code and knew the target and the likely date, while the Japanese remained largely unaware of their opponent's strength and positions even after the battle began.

All four Japanese fleet carriers present were sunk, three of them within minutes of the dive-bomber attacks that began at 10:22 on 4 June, while the American torpedo squadrons lost most of their aircraft without scoring a hit.
Japan lost about 3,000 men and many well-trained pilots, and its ability to replace losses in materiel and men became insufficient as American industrial and training capacity grew.
dyk: Yorktown, damaged at the Coral Sea a month before and expected to need months of repair, was made battle-ready at Pearl Harbor in 72 hours, with repair crews still aboard when she sailed.
ev: Yamamoto's plan to take Midway and destroy the American carriers is adopted after the Doolittle Raid on Tokyo
American code breakers confirm that the Japanese objective "AF" is Midway and give the attack date as 4 or 5 June
Midway-based aircraft find the Japanese occupation force, and the Japanese attack on the Aleutians begins
Nagumo's aircraft bomb Midway at about 06:34, and American torpedo squadrons attack the carriers without success
American dive bombers set Kaga, Sōryū and Akagi ablaze from 10:22
Hiryū's two strikes cripple Yorktown, and in the afternoon American bombers leave Hiryū burning
Yamamoto orders a general withdrawal to the west
Mikuma is sunk and Yorktown capsizes after submarine torpedoes

f.date: 4–7 June 1942; the Japanese Aleutian operation began a day earlier, on 3 June
f.place: The sea near Midway Atoll, about 1,300 miles (2,100 km) north-west of Oahu in the Hawaiian chain, in the North Pacific
f.sides: The United States Pacific Fleet under Admiral Chester Nimitz, with carrier groups under Frank Jack Fletcher and Raymond Spruance and 122 aircraft on Midway; the Japanese Combined Fleet under Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto, with the carrier strike force (Kidō Butai) under Chūichi Nagumo, which sailed with 248 aircraft on four carriers
f.outcome: The Japanese lost the carriers Akagi, Kaga, Sōryū and Hiryū and the heavy cruiser Mikuma, and 3,057 men; the United States lost the carrier Yorktown, the destroyer Hammann and 307 men. Japan did not take Midway.
